title: Folder listings — what a location holds, as of when someone asked
note:
ONE RECORD PER LOCATION, filed by the mini-worker's `list-folders` action (card RV-18c (lane inbox listing), 2026-09-09, widened by RV-21 (list a location) the same day, platform/workers/mini-worker/review_folder.py) so a form can offer a SELECT or a FILTER instead of a text field somebody spells differently from the way the warehouse did. THE ITEM ID IS THE LOCATION. IT IS A SNAPSHOT, NOT HISTORY, AND THAT IS THE OPPOSITE OF ITS NEIGHBOUR: `review` records are events and are appended forever, while a re-list REPLACES that location's listing — the writer removes the location's earlier records (head AND parts) after writing the new ones, so the plane holds exactly one listing per location. This is written down here because a later hand will read `records/` as append-only and want to 'fix' it, and the fix would fold three stale listings into one dropdown that offers folders which are gone. `serve_records` is deliberately ABSENT (latest write wins per reviewer+item), which is the same statement made to the API. ON DEMAND, NEVER ON A TICK (the developer, ruled 2026-09-09, "and the tick should be on-demand listing"): a form files a request, the worker answers that one request, and a location nobody asked about is never read — there is no schedule and no recurring job anywhere in this path. STALENESS IS BOUNDED BY WHEN THE PERSON LAST ASKED, so `taken` is load-bearing: the form shows it beside the control, and RV-18d (subfolder select) sets no age threshold because a form cannot know a location's rate of change. NOT THE `review` KIND, on purpose: a listing is not a review event, and the review manifest is frozen with a grammar (event, type, asset, reviewers, verdict, decision) that a fourth non-event shape would quietly empty out. It is PLUMBING, filed beside `infer-runs` — not the batch-request vocabulary the email lead curates. READ-ONLY, ABSOLUTELY: every Drive listing goes through the READ-ONLY reader service account on the same `drive.readonly` scope and the same list call RV-18 (folder inventory) already makes, and every repo listing reads names and sizes without opening a file; nothing on this path writes to Drive or to the tree it lists. POINTERS, NEVER BYTES (workspace rule 3): a row is a name, an id or a path and a size — no file is opened and no media is copied. A LOCATION THAT CANNOT BE LISTED IS SAID IN WORDS AND NEVER AS AN EMPTY LIST: a lane with no inbox is SKIPPED BY NAME on a record of its own, and every other failure REFUSES with a named reason and files nothing, because an absent record and an empty list are both read as 'the folder is not there', which is a different and false statement. NO BROWSER EVER CALLS DRIVE — the board reads these records through the records API it already polls.

THREE SHAPES, ONE ACTION AND ONE KIND (RV-21 (list a location), 2026-09-09). `shape` says which: `drive-folders` (the subfolders of the ONE Reviews folder, or — for a request that names no `warehouse` — RV-18c's original per-lane listing, answered byte for byte as it always was), `drive-files` (one subfolder's files as {name, id, type, bytes}, the call the form's checklist cannot exist without), `repo` (a directory's entries AND the flat markdown list under it). THE FLAT LIST IS THE PRIMARY CONTROL AND A MEASUREMENT CHOSE IT: over the real tree — 444 directories, 1,127 markdown names under the four declared roots — reaching a typical md file by drilling took a MEDIAN OF 5 list calls (21% within three, 100% only by six) against drill-down's own stated kill of about three, so the filter over the flat list leads and `entries` is the secondary control for browsing when the name is not known. Do not re-promote drill-down because serving the flat list is harder.

A LOCATION'S ROWS ARE SPLIT ACROSS RECORDS, NEVER TRUNCATED. ~1,100 paths exceed the plane's 16 KB verdict cap (WM-25 (verdict cap one source)), so the HEAD record (item = the location id) holds the rows inline when the whole stream fits and holds `parts` — the item ids of the PART records, `<location>-p001`, `<location>-e001`, in order — when it does not. It always says which, and `total` is the whole count either way, so a reader checks it has them all rather than trusting that it does. A part record carries `part`, `index`, `of` and `parts_total` and is a FRAGMENT, not a short listing. A form that reads only the head of a split listing is filtering over a list that lies, which is the exact failure the split exists to avoid.

ALLOWED REPO ROOTS, RULED BY the developer 2026-09-09: new-workflow-design/, components/, team/, platform/. A path outside them is refused BY NAME. The set moves by a ruling, never by a maker widening it to make a test pass; it lives as one constant in review_folder.py and the declared test asserts exactly those four.

verdict_fields.note: the worker action that filed it — the same word the request record carries. STILL ONE WORD after RV-21 (list a location): three shapes are answered by one action, and the name was kept rather than renamed because renaming it would have changed RV-18c (lane inbox listing)'s behaviour, which the widening card forbids.
exactly one per record; reserved so a later event on this kind can join it without changing what a listing means

`skipped` means a lane has NO inbox folder configured in platform/data/review-drive.json — a named skip, never an error and never an absent record. A Drive failure, a path outside the declared roots and a location that does not exist are none of these three: they REFUSE, file nothing, and the request record carries the reason in words (a wall a person must take down is never turned into an emptiness).

WHICH OF THE THREE (RV-21). Absent on RV-18c's original per-lane listing, which is unchanged and carries `lane`/`inbox`/`folders` instead — that record shape is frozen, and a reader tells the two apart by this field's presence.

where the location lives — the same word `asset.warehouse` uses on the review kind, so a row composed from a listing needs no translation. The two are the only two the form offers (the developer, 2026-09-09: "we limit options for where it lives to just repo and google drive for now").

the location IN WORDS: the Reviews folder's title, the subfolder's name, the repo path, or "the four declared roots". What a person reads on the record and in the status line; the item id is what machinery matches on.

RV-18c's per-lane listing ONLY — the lane whose inbox this is, the record's item id, and the ONLY lane read. No lane is ever listed that was not asked for. ABSENT on every RV-21 shape: there is one Reviews folder and no lane concept (the developer, 2026-09-09, "I dont think we need the concept of a lane for now").
the Drive folder id that was listed, READ from platform/data/review-drive.json and never a second copy of it. null when a lane was skipped; absent on the repo and drive-files shapes.

WHEN THE LISTING WAS TAKEN, UTC. Not bookkeeping: the form shows it beside the control, because a snapshot with no stamp is a claim about now that nobody checked. Every part record carries the SAME stamp as its head — the parts are one listing, not several.
how many rows are IN THIS RECORD. On a head whose rows were split out to parts this is 0 and `total` is the real number — read `total` for the size of the list.

how many rows the location holds ALTOGETHER, across the head and every part. The number a reader checks its own sum against; a form whose parts do not add up to this has not read the whole list and must say so rather than filter over what it got.

the rows of the shape's own row grammar: drive-folders [{name, id, modified}], drive-files [{name, id, type, bytes}], repo [{path, bytes}] — the FLAT MARKDOWN LIST, which is the primary control. Inline on the head when the whole stream fits the 16 KB cap, EMPTY on the head when `parts` names the records that carry them. Never a truncated prefix of the list: a filter over a truncated list is a filter that lies. In drive-files a null `type` means no panel renders that file — it is a ROW so the form can tick it off and disable it with the reason in words, never an omission, because a file that vanishes from a listing reads as a file that is not there.
the item ids of the records carrying `rows`, in order, or [] when the rows are inline. `<location>-p001`, `<location>-p002`, … Read them all or say you did not.
what this record IS. `head` is the one a form reads first; `rows` and `entries` are FRAGMENTS of a split stream and are not listings on their own.
part records only: which part this is, 1-based.
part records only: the item id of the head this part belongs to.
part records only: how many parts that stream has, so a part found alone says how much of the list is missing.

RV-18c's per-lane listing ONLY: the rows, [{name, id, modified}] in name order. The RV-21 shapes carry the same grammar under `rows`. POINTERS, NEVER BYTES: no file inside a subfolder is opened, listed or served from here.

drive-folders only: how many LOOSE FILES the listed folder held. Counted, not offered — a person picks a folder — and stated rather than dropped in silence, so 'my file is not in the list' has an answer on the record.
drive-files only: the subfolder's NAME as the request gave it, or null when the request gave an id instead.
drive-files only: the Drive id of the subfolder whose files these are — the id shape 1's own rows carry, so the form needs no second lookup.
drive-files only: how many NESTED FOLDERS the subfolder held. Counted for the same reason loose files are: a number on the record answers 'where did my file go' without a second call.
repo only: the path the flat markdown list covers, or `*` for all four declared roots. The listing's own scope, stated on the record, because a filter is only honest about the tree it was given.

repo only: the location directory's immediate children, [{name, kind}] with kind `dir` or `file`, in name order — the SECONDARY control, for browsing when the name is not known. Inline when they fit, [] when `entry_parts` names the records that carry them. At the top location the entries are the four declared roots.

repo only: the item ids of the records carrying `entries`, `<location>-e001`… , or [] when they are inline. Split for the same reason rows are — one directory in this repo holds over 2,500 entries, so this is not theoretical.
repo only: how many entries the directory holds altogether, across the head and every entry part.

[{lane, reason, detail}] — the lanes named as skipped rather than errored or silently absent. Today the only reason is `no-inbox`. Empty on every listed location and on every RV-21 shape, which refuse by name instead.
the writer's version, `folder-listing/<n>`. `folder-listing/1` is RV-18c's per-lane listing, unchanged; `folder-listing/2` is RV-21's three-shape writer.
